references.text: Mentions the Sea of Kinnereth (Sea of Galilee) at the eastern border, the same geographical reference as in Joshua 12:3
Describes the Arabah valley, the Sea of Kinnereth, and the Salt Sea (Dead Sea) as boundary markers, identical geographical references
Mentions the Arabah valley by the Salt Sea and the slopes at Pisgah, the same place name as in Joshua 12:3
Mentions the summit of Pisgah and the view over the wilderness (Jeshimoth), a geographical connection to Beth-Jeshimoth
Mentions Beth-Jeshimoth by the plains of Moab at the Jordan, the same place mentioned in Joshua 12:3
Mentions Kinnerot and Arabah as geographical areas in the description of the kings who were defeated
Mentions Beth-Jeshimoth and the slopes at Pisgah as part of the inheritance of the tribe of Reuben
The first mention of the Salt Sea (Dead Sea) in the Bible, the same geographical reference
